optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Predictive Maintenance Engineer, Wind Turbine Fleet Analytics
professionalSummary: Seasoned engineer with three years of experience deploying and operating failure models for wind turbine fleets, ensuring high alert precision and robust incident management.
experienceHighlights: Deployed four gearbox and bearing failure models into the live scoring service, each released via the platform team's pipeline and tracked with dedicated release tickets.
Monitored live alert precision weekly against confirmed failures, maintaining accuracy through continuous review with maintenance planners.
Handled production incidents, including two sensor feed drop-outs, documenting responses in the platform incident log.
Coordinated model releases with the platform team, clearly delineating responsibilities in release tickets.
Authored comprehensive model cards detailing training windows, backtest results, known limitations, and hand‑over conditions.
projectsAndWorkSamples: Release tickets for four models (source: src_bbd795e6fdae, src_95582ab44bf2).
Weekly precision review records (source: src_142b77c79acc, src_95582ab44bf2).
Incident records for two sensor feed drop-outs (source: src_142b77c79acc, src_95582ab44bf2).
optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The provided resume and work samples establish the candidate’s deployment, monitoring, incident handling, release coordination, and documentation activities for failure models in a wind turbine fleet analytics context. They do not provide evidence of experience beyond the four gearbox and bearing models or of work with other turbine components or broader fleet analytics responsibilities.

decisionBoundary.statement: Candidate meets all listed requirements based on documented evidence; human review recommended to confirm fit and assess broader competencies.

role.roleTitle: Predictive Maintenance Engineer, Wind Turbine Fleet Analytics

evidence.text: Deployed four gearbox and bearing failure models into the live scoring service of the fleet analytics platform over three years, releasing each through the platform team's release pipeline under my own release tickets.
evidence.notes: Direct statement of deployment and live scoring integration.

evidence.text: Watched live alert precision against confirmed failures in the weekly review with the maintenance planners.
handled the production model incidents in that period, including two sensor feed drop-outs, with incident records in the platform incident log.
Coordinated model releases with the platform team in the release review, recording in the release ticket which checks were mine and which belonged to the platform team.
Built and backtested each model on the historical sensor and work-order data under the evaluation protocol agreed with the planners before proposing it for release.
Wrote the model card for each model, listing the training data window, the backtest results, the known limitations for turbines without vibration sensors and the hand-over conditions.
